question: Why does an OLED phone screen throw away more than half of its own light?
answer: To stop it acting as a mirror. Behind every pixel lies a metal electrode that reflects room light and would wash out the blacks. A circular polarizer on top blocks it, and also over half the pixels' own light. Samsung's polarizer-free design, first used in the 2021 Galaxy Z Fold3, let through 33% more.
